motto: Serving Greywater Falls since 1887, and the lake somewhat longer.
weather: Clear and cold, 31°F, a thin skin of ice at the shallow edge of the lake for the first time all season

undercurrent.phenomenon: The name has crossed from ledger to daylight congregation to standing patron; the fourteen-year card itself is now retired and filed, the town's remaining work simply letting the closed file stay closed.
undercurrent.note: Crest exhale continues past the hundredth edition into its natural close: the card is closed, Russ's file is closed, Toby logged a full porch sentence (his log nearly complete), first shore ice marks the season turning conventional again. Remaining threads for coda: Russ's folded riddle (still unopened, likely stays that way as his resolution), Toby's notebook (one more small entry could finish it), Agnes's declared silence (holding, steer to pure weather-talk), the sixth cup and free bread now simply fixtures. Hold level dropping through high 30s toward low-to-mid 30s over the next few days, aiming for coda around day 26-28 of the season (day 105-107 overall).

editor.name: Wren Aldercott
editor.voice: Dry, precise, allergic to drama, which is unfortunate given recent events. Writes like a person holding a clipboard while standing in rising water. Lets one true thing slip per edition, usually in the last line.

season_arc.premise: Calloway finishes reshelving the east alcove in the last cataloguer's 2009 order and finds, tucked behind where the ninth book sat, a library card checked out that same interrupted Wednesday and never returned. It is due back today. The borrower's name is nobody currently living in Greywater Falls has ever heard of, and the little pocket calendar stamped inside has fourteen years of due-date stamps on it already, one for every year since, each in a different hand.
